groupings.title: Get the app on a device
groupings.description: Hand it a Play Store link and it works out the package, checks whether the emulator can actually install anything, and gets the app running — or names exactly which wall you hit.

groupings.title: Drive it and take it apart
groupings.description: The agent-shaped loop: a screen becomes a dozen numbered rows instead of 24KB of XML, taps target text rather than pixels, and assertions fail loudly with what was really on screen.

groupings.title: Review the whole app
groupings.description: Point it at a Play link and get a bounded, evidence-backed report — every finding tied to a screenshot, every skipped area named, and the app's own on-screen text treated as data rather than instructions.

groupings.title: Show it, don't tell it
groupings.description: Record the app driving itself and burn explanation cards straight into the MP4 — because you cannot overlay a third-party Android app, the captions are stamped live and composited afterwards.

groupings.title: What the store and the wire say
groupings.description: Read an app's public Play listing — rating, reviews, installs, changelog — and capture which servers it actually contacts, all without owning the app or rooting the device.

groupings.title: Is the UI any good
groupings.description: A UX/UI heuristic audit: it measures touch targets and screen-reader-invisible controls from the accessibility tree, judges the twelve usability categories against fixed thresholds, and scores findings by severity — no laundered overall grade.
